score_status: Provisional judgments; no raster or runtime validation

fields.movement_initiator: The upper chest commits toward the intended action; pelvis and supports visibly catch that commitment. This is a relation among authored keys, never a delayed movement input.
fields.body_part_delay: The trailing shoulder and non-grip forearm respond after the chest; pelvis catch precedes final wrist/flame settling. Offsets compress or disappear when a state is too short.
fields.center_of_gravity: Projected mass approaches the front support and briefly outruns it during exertion; the next actual support restores balance. Quiet stance stays believable rather than permanently pitched.
fields.shoulder_rhythm: One shoulder reaches farther and returns later, with restrained counterrotation on the other side. Contact temporarily interrupts the alternating rhythm.
fields.pelvis_rhythm: The pelvis follows chest commitment, loads the support and returns under the torso. It has less excursion than the chest and still responds to the alternating legs.
fields.arm_rhythm: The action/grip arm reaches with intent; the other participates unevenly as a counterweight or protective check. No rigid rear arm, twin elbows or automatic mirrored half-cycle.
fields.leg_rhythm: A complete alternating cycle with brisk recovery to catch the forward mass, traceable knees and feet, and distinct load versus airborne moments. Unequal performance must still have credible supports.
fields.idle_identity: A small unfinished inclination to act, checked by the pelvis/support before it becomes a stride; one elbow settles later. Restraint makes the next commitment noticeable.
fields.locomotion_identity: The person appears slightly ahead of their own balance: hurried support recovery follows torso commitment. Desperation comes from timing and restoration, not a trained sprint wedge.
fields.attack_identity: A too-eager connected reach or bodily shove, with supported forward contact and recognizable grip. No expert guard, long punch windup or new strike type.
fields.recovery_identity: The action overshoots its comfortable reach, then the support and pelvis retrieve the torso; the returning arm follows. Confirmed contact rebounds; a whiff exposes the overreach.
fields.gameplay_risk: A leading chest can falsely suggest early hit reach or movement startup. Keep root and damage windows authoritative; body excursion must not promise contact before active time.
fields.animation_risk: At native size the chase of chest/pelvis can become constant falling, shirt drift or foot slide. Needs conservative volume, clear support changes and actual transition testing.
fields.genericness_risk: A constant forward lean would reduce this to the familiar action runner. The defining behavior is commitment followed by a visible catch across idle/run/contact/recovery, with quiet counterposes.

fields.movement_initiator: Support loading and pelvis drive initiate exertion; the ribcage initially protects itself, then opens into the action. These drawings track existing acceleration and contact rather than adding a pause.
fields.body_part_delay: Chest opening trails pelvic drive; the free elbow loosens after the shoulder, while the grip wrist remains connected. At contact, protective recoil precedes loose secondary settling.
fields.center_of_gravity: Mass stays comparatively near the loaded support and travels forward in short commitment; the body quickly recontains it. Avoid an implausible perfectly centered mass in every running frame.
fields.shoulder_rhythm: One shoulder remains higher/nearer the neck during preparation while the other opens into motion, then both release unequally. This must read as protection, not a combat guard.
fields.pelvis_rhythm: Support alternation leads restrained pelvic tilt/turn; ribcage turn follows at a different amplitude. The pelvis provides a readable base for the short body drive.
fields.arm_rhythm: One arm remains compact while the other helps balance or maintains the grip. Neither is frozen; small unequal releases prevent a robot or held boxing guard.
fields.leg_rhythm: Full alternating contacts with efficient passing and a perceptible loaded/down phase. A support-driven rhythm permits an awkward first push without a distinct slow walk mechanic.
fields.idle_identity: Uneven protective enclosure around the torso with a small release of tension rather than full symmetrical breathing. Weight rests on one credible support without a heroic wide stance.
fields.locomotion_identity: A contained, urgent run: legs drive and the protected chest reluctantly opens. Stress is conveyed by constrained arm use and torso compensation rather than luxurious stride extension.
fields.attack_identity: A short supported bodily drive into forearm/shove-like contact, followed by involuntary reclosure. The flame can exaggerate confidence while the physical body remains apprehensive.
fields.recovery_identity: The chest closes and mass returns to support before elbows and clothing settle. Contact recoil differs from an empty shove while preserving the same protective person.
fields.gameplay_risk: A brace can look like slow startup or a blocking ability. Show it within current clocks, without waiting, shield cues, reduced damage or control lock.
fields.animation_risk: Compact arms and dark torso can merge at 1×; an overly low pelvis becomes constant crouching. Requires a strong elbow gap, visible wrist/grip and alternating leg ownership.
fields.genericness_risk: Protective posture can drift into armored ninja, fighter guard or old stock hunch. Keep civilian apprehension and release, body-driven gait, modest stance and consequential recovery.

fields.movement_initiator: A diagonal ribcage twist stores apparent intent against a briefly resisting pelvis; the body unwinds toward the action. No rotational delay may alter actual movement or attack startup.
fields.body_part_delay: Pelvis and the trailing shoulder resolve after the ribcage turn; arms take unequal crossing paths and release later. This creates more overlap relationships than the short clocks may support.
fields.center_of_gravity: Mass moves diagonally across support before projecting forward; unwind can leave it off center until the returning foot/body catches it. Static and airborne requirements must remain distinct.
fields.shoulder_rhythm: Pronounced unequal forward/back shoulder motion, with changes in which plane is exposed. Compression and release would have to remain readable after horizontal mirroring.
fields.pelvis_rhythm: Counterturn rather than matching shoulder turn, followed by a smaller delayed unwind into the new support. Waist connection is essential, not a swiveling cutout joint.
fields.arm_rhythm: One arm initially folds across the torso while the other trails, then they separate along unequal arcs. Grip ownership must remain anatomical even when the arms overlap.
fields.leg_rhythm: Alternating support carries the torso's diagonal action, with uneven passing accents and a corrective gather. No lateral gameplay step or new stance transition is permitted.
fields.idle_identity: A residual uneven twist held between chest and pelvis, released by a small support adjustment. Avoid an unexplained perpetual snake-like sway.
fields.locomotion_identity: Urgent running with a restrained winding/unwinding torso accent across contacts. Its rhythm is distinct on paper but risks concealing travel direction and leg phase.
fields.attack_identity: Awkward diagonal unwind into existing forward contact, followed by an imbalanced return. A rotational flourish must not suggest a spin attack, martial skill or broader hitbox.
fields.recovery_identity: Counterturn checks the initial unwind, then support and limbs gather. Excess reversal could consume the entire 80 ms recovery and leave no readable restored key.
fields.gameplay_risk: Changing visible torso planes can miscue facing, reach and contact during a short startup. Crossed arms can conceal the existing held weapon and direction.
fields.animation_risk: Frequent occlusion swaps, foreshortening and mirror constraints are difficult to author consistently at roughly 56 px body height; no native proof exists to support feasibility.
fields.genericness_risk: Strong shape contrast can still become a stock stylish fighter or serpentine motion gimmick. A habitual twist is not by itself a civilian identity.
